text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- The ruling coalition led by Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto has finalised its strategy if the Lahore High Court reinstates ousted chief minister Manzoor Wattoo.
- Nepal and Pakistan on Saturday signed two agreements designed to enhance bilateral economic and political cooperation between the two countries.
- The Saudi Turkey Bin Abdullah Group's president met Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto and told her about plans to invest heavily in aviation and oil refinery sectors of Pakistan.
- Businessmen and experts in a seminar proposed a cautious and phased approach towards resumption of normal trade with India.
BUISNESS RECORDER

- The state-run National Investment Trust has sought permission from the State (central) Bank to borrow up to seven billion rupees from commercial banks for improving its liquidity position and enlarging the fund's base.
- The federal government may allow operations of close-end mutual funds without going public.
- Pakistan has approved four contracts with U.S.-based companies worth about $88.2 million for oil and gas exploration, sources said.
- The consumption of furnace oil has come down by 25 to 30 percent by major consumers excluding the power sector following the recent 10 percent price rise.
- The federal government has decided in principle to restore cellular phone services in Karachi from January 1997, sources said.
- Polyster staple fibre prices have risen by nine rupees to 81 rupees per kg since November 2, on strong demand in the international markets.
FINANCIAL POST
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan has assumed the authority to sanction and disburse credit to all public sector corporations to control excess money being pumped into the system.
THE NEWS
- The Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry, which had announced it would observe Sunday as a weekly holiday, has reverted to the Friday holiday.
THE MUSLIM
- The Pakistan Bar Council, the apex body of lawyers, has said that the prime minister's advice in the appointment of judges by the president was binding and a constitutional requirement.
THE FRONTIER POST

- The government has sought technical cooperation from the International Monetary Fund for creating a transparent system for collecting and monitoring revenue collection, as well as calculating the deficit and inflation rate.
THE NATION

- The state-run Private Power and Infrastructure Board has halted the implementation of agreements over seven private sector power projects which had failed to attract financial backing within a stipulated period.
-- Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
